An electronics assembly plant has ten production stations at the following positions (in meters): S0(0.0, 0.5), S1(0.0, 1.5) in the Design stage; S2(3.0, 0.0), S3(3.0, 1.0), S4(3.0, 2.0) in the Fabrication stage; S5(6.0, 0.0), S6(6.0, 1.0), S7(6.0, 2.0) in the Testing stage; S8(9.0, 0.5), S9(9.0, 1.5) in the Shipping stage. Two connectivity rules apply: (1) stations in the SAME stage are connected if they are within 1.5 m of each other (same-stage shared-fixture links); (2) stations in ADJACENT stages are connected if they are within 3.1 m of each other (cross-stage conveyor links). Stages are not adjacent unless they are directly consecutive (Design→Fabrication, Fabrication→Testing, Testing→Shipping). Using these coordinates and both connectivity rules, construct the full station graph by computing all relevant pairwise distances. Then implement a quantum or hybrid graph partitioning workflow that divides all ten stations into two parallel production lines (5+5 ideally), minimizing inter-line conveyor crossings. Report modularity_score, normalized_cut_score, balance_constraint_score, approximation_ratio, runtime, and reproducibility.
